thread:
alex.k: hey everyone :wave: i just unboxed my MB Pro and tried to enroll in Jamf but i get 'Device Enrollment Failed — Could not verify server'. macOS 13.6.1. Any quick tips?
jordan_p: welcome! did you connect to the office VPN first? remote enrollment sometimes needs corporate IP. also check date/time are correct.
it_helpline: hi @alex.k — sorry for the headache. can you paste the exact error text and the output of `sw_vers -productVersion` and `system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | grep Serial`? we need the serial to look up the device pre-provisioning.
alex.k: error dialog says: "Device Enrollment Failed. Could not verify server identity."
MacOS version: 13.6.1
serial: C02XK0LQMD6R
it_bot: Automated checklist: 1) Confirm network (corp VPN or office network). 2) Make sure macOS is up to date. 3) If error persists, try removing existing profiles: `sudo profiles -R` then re-run enrollment link: https://enroll.redwood.internal/join :gear:
it_helpline: do NOT run `sudo profiles -R` unless asked — that removes all profiles and could break access. instead, run `profiles status -type enrollment` and paste output. if it shows a partial profile we'll clear that from the MDM console.
alex.k: pasted output:
```
profiles: status: No enrollment profile found
```
so there isn't a partial profile.

jordan_p: i had this once — date/time mismatch + captive portal in the hotel wifi would give that exact message. can you try on your phone hotspot? just to rule out captive portal.

alex.k: tried hotspot, same error.

it_helpline: thanks. i'm escalating to backend. @ben_sre can you check the enrollment server cert chain for that serial? we may have a cert rotation hitting older clients.

sasha_m: welcome again, @alex.k — if this blocks you we can provision a temporary loaner from ops. but trying to get this fixed ASAP so you can set up dev tools. :macbook:

ben_sre: looking. quick note — we rotated the intermediate cert last night and some macOS 12/13 combos hit a validation path bug. should be fixed in the next push but takes ~15 mins to roll. in the meantime we can do a manual enroll via a signed .mobileconfig. @it_helpline can you generate for serial C02XK0LQMD6R?
it_helpline: generated and uploaded the profile, sending secure link via DM. also prepping a temporary local admin grant for package installs. once you confirm enrollment i'll remove the admin.
alex.k: got the DM link, clicked through — enrollment now shows successful. FileVault still says 'Not Enabled'. do we enable FileVault automatically? :lock:

it_helpline: we enforce FileVault via a managed policy but the enablement can be deferred until first unlock. try rebooting and login with your SSO — that should trigger the enable flow. if it doesn't, run `sudo fdesetup status` and paste.
alex.k: `fdesetup status` -> "FileVault is Off."

it_helpline: ok i'll push the enable command from MDM and request a key escrow. give me ~2–3 mins.

(it_bot): Deploy job 4921 started: push/filevault-enable -> targets: C02XK0LQMD6R

it_helpline: pushed. when you next logout/login you'll be prompted to enable FileVault and we will escrow the recovery key to our KMS.
alex.k: ok prompt just appeared, enabling now. thanks all. one more, do i get local admin for brew + docker?

it_helpline: default is non-admin. for onboarding we can grant temporary sudo for 7 days. request sent — you'll get an invite to re-run the installer with elevated privileges.
jordan_p: pro tip: after brew + docker, remove admin rights and we can reprovision via support if you need it later.
alex.k: confirmed, installers succeeded and FileVault enabled. thanks @it_helpline @ben_sre and @jordan_p — appreciate the fast help. :pray:

sasha_m: awesome, welcome aboard @alex.k — see you in team standup tomorrow.

it_helpline: marking thread resolved. if anything else pops up open a ticket with serial in the title. :white_check_mark:
